title: Probe-driven kernel selection for prefill pipelining and attention tiling
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Problem: The runtime currently selects kernels using static heuristics derived from offline profiling aggregated by architecture and coarse sequence-length buckets. This leaves suboptimal choices for workloads with mixed sequence-length distributions, variable attention patterns (long prefix + short decode), and diverse GPU microarchitectures. We see tail latency and cost regressions when model inputs diverge from the profiled distribution.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight, per-request micro-probing phase during prefill that runs a few targeted kernel micro-benchmarks (micro-ops) to measure: memory copy bandwidth, soft attentiveness / attention tile throughput for the current sequence-length window, and KV-cache read/write latency. Use these probe signals combined with an on-device small sequence-length predictor to select a kernel variant and attention tiling strategy for the remainder of the request. The probe must be sub-millisecond amortized across tokens and safe to run in the critical path for the first prefill batch only.

Key ideas: 1) Micro-probe runner: a tiny harness executed on-request that runs 2-3 representative microkernels with capped iterations and returns a normalized score. 2) Probe cache: cache probe results keyed by (GPU-fingerprint, model-arch-fingerprint, short-prefill-hash) for quick reuse across nearby requests. 3) Warm-start prefetch: use probe to decide whether to prefetch larger KV slices or use chunked streaming to reduce decode memory pressure. 4) Attention tiling selector: pick between tiled-shared, tiled-private, and fused attention depending on measured bandwidth and seq-len projection. 5) Safe fallback: if probe fails or returns noisy data, fall back to current architecture-default kernel.

Why different from existing autotuners: instead of a large offline autotuner that builds heavy cost models, this approach trades off some probing overhead for per-request adaptation, benefiting heterogenous fleets and mixed workloads (e.g., chat apps where users send varied-length contexts). It complements the existing kernel portfolio manager by providing a fast probe-feedback loop for immediate kernel selection and a short-term cache for repeated patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Probe overhead < 0.8ms median on p4d and a100-80GB across representative models when amortized over first prefill batch
End-to-end p50 token latency improved by >=8% on 3 mixed-distribution workloads compared to static heuristic baseline
p95 tail latency no worse than baseline (within 3%) across benchmark suite
Probe cache TTL and eviction policy integrated with existing routing cache; cache hit rate > 60% for production chat traces
Failsafe: if probe result confidence < threshold, runtime uses architecture-default kernel and logs event
Unit and integration tests for probe runner, cache, and selector with simulated noisy signals
technical_notes: Probe micro-benchmarks: memcpy bandwidth (4KB..1MB), small-attention tile throughput (seq=64..512 simulated with reduced heads), kv-rd/wr latency using pinned pages
Score normalization: z-score relative to architecture baseline collected during onboarding to avoid inter-GPU variance
Seq-len predictor: lightweight logistic model (features: recent request length, user-specified max_context, rolling mean token length) trained offline and embedded as small coefficients in runtime
Cache key: sha1(gpu_fingerprint + model_hash + seq_len_bucket + kernel_family). TTL=5 minutes, LRU with size cap by shard
Telemetry: expose probe_ok, probe_latency_ms, selected_kernel, selection_confidence, cache_hit boolean on per-request tracing
Safety: probes execute on same CUDA stream as prefill to avoid extra synchronization; use non-blocking timers and guard with watchdog to preempt overrun
